ctx.x: When did you first work with Claude Williams?
Well, truthfully, the first time I worked with Claude Williams, it was about 1969 or 1970.
I wondered about that. So you hadn't worked with him earlier.

items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: I was with Jay McShann. We played a blues festival in Chicago.

ctx.x: Oh, well I knew Buddy from Texas or wherever he was from. And I ran into him because I was down there with a band, a territory band down there by name of Alphonso Trent. He was the first black band that played in the Adolphus Hotel in Dallas. And he was pretty well known all over Texas, Alphonso, so Buddy had worked with Alphonso around there in Texas. Something happened and the band finally broke up. And then T. Holder was down there with a different group. And he had picked up Buddy. And we played together in…

but all musicians who are supposed to be from 65 up, you know. They call it “elder statesmen.” So I had Buddy to come over, and went over in New York, and his picture is on one thing. We made him blow a few tunes and I made him play on one tune on the tape, but he’s still weak you know, kind of sick. We had Buddy one night, it must have been about five or six years ago, I was with Jay McShann. We played a blues festival in Chicago. We had Buddy, he’d been sick then, but we brought him out on the stage and set him…

items.title: Jay McShann interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: Well it’s nice to see you reunited with Spoon and the Fiddler.

ctx.x: Well I don’t know. I guess I’ll just roll with the punches, whatever happens you know, is. I guess that’s the way I explain it.
Well it’s nice to see you reunited with Spoon and the Fiddler.
